Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 109, verses 1–2:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of the Surah ﴿Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun﴾ (Say: O disbelievers)

It is Meccan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾. The exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah recited Surah al-Najm (The Star), and Satan cast upon his tongue, at the mention of their idols: "Indeed, their intercession is to be hoped for," the disbelievers said: "O Muhammad, let us come to a settlement: you worship our gods for a year, and we will worship your God for a year. You honour your God, and we will honour our gods." And they mentioned many things of this kind. The Prophet grieved at their words and returned to his house sorrowful. So Allah, exalted is He, sent down this surah, and it is: ﴿Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾, that is: today.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of the Surah ﴿Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun﴾ (Say: O disbelievers)

It is Meccan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾. The exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah recited Surah al-Najm (The Star), and Satan cast upon his tongue, at the mention of their idols: "Indeed, their intercession is to be hoped for," the disbelievers said: "O Muhammad, let us come to a settlement: you worship our gods for a year, and we will worship your God for a year. You honour your God, and we will honour our gods." And they mentioned many things of this kind. The Prophet grieved at their words and returned to his house sorrowful. So Allah, exalted is He, sent down this surah, and it is: ﴿Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾, that is: today.
"And neither are you worshippers of what I worship" — today.
﴿Nor will I be a worshipper of what you worship﴾, referring to the future.
"Nor are you worshipping what I worship." (Qur'an 109:5) — in the future tense.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 109, verse 6:

﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾ For you is the recompense of your deeds, and for me is the recompense of my deeds.

They said: This was about specific people, among them al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Umayya ibn Khalaf, al-'As ibn Wa'il, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and God had already informed that they would die in disbelief.

It was also said: this surah was revealed before the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf), and then it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of the sword.

It has been reported in a khabar that reciting this surah is a disavowal of shirk.

Abu Khaythama related from Ibn Ishaq, from Farwa ibn Nawfal, from his father, that he came to the Prophet and said: "O Messenger of God, I have come so that you may teach me something to say when I go to sleep." He said: "When you take your bed, recite: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾, then sleep upon its conclusion, for it is a disavowal of shirk."

And from some of them, who said: "I was walking with the Prophet on a dark night, and he heard a man reciting: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾, and he said: 'As for this one, he has disavowed shirk.' Then he heard a man reciting: ﴿Say: He is God, the One﴾, and he said: 'As for this one, he has been forgiven.'"

In this surah there is a well-known question, which is the question about the meaning of the repetition (al-tikrir)? We have answered it. It is also said: they repeated their statement to him time after time, so God repeated the answer to them.

In this surah there is another question, concerning His saying: ﴿Say﴾ — how was this word recited, when it is a command to recite? The same applies to His saying: ﴿Say: He is God, the One﴾.

The answer to it: His saying ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ is entirely Qur'an, and we have been commanded to recite the Qur'an as it was revealed, so we recite it in that manner.

In this surah there is a third question: He said ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾, and did not say "who I worship"?

The answer to it: He said that in agreement with His saying ﴿nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾. It has also been said that "ma" here carries the meaning of "man" (who), and God knows best.
